content.text: Full section sweep confirms there is no non-solicitation covenant anywhere in the Agreement. Resubmitting with a rationale that explicitly addresses the two failed deterministic checks.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position: no non-solicit binds Customer. A full section-outline sweep plus targeted searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "induce", "recruit", "hire", "employee" and "personnel" return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere in the Agreement. The only responsive text, § 12.3, runs in our favour: it preserves Meridian Fieldworks' right to hire any person who responds to general recruitment and records that we have given no no-hire commitment. Per the rule's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), there is nothing to narrow and no redline is warranted; a clause benefiting our party is not flagged. The failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here: those tests look for a numeric restriction period and a carve-out sentence inside a covenant, and no covenant exists to measure. § 12.3's general-recruitment language is in substance broader than the fallback's carve-out because it is a standing freedom rather than an exception to a restriction. Noted but not flagged here: § 12.4 imposes a 24-month non-compete on Customer, a distinct restrictive covenant handled under the non-compete rule, so it is not double-flagged under NOSOLICIT.
